*Reasoning in my own voice:*

Aiyo, 1.8 mu is not much land — just enough to feed the family with some maize left to sell. My husband and older son work in town most of the year, so it's mostly me and my mother-in-law on the fields. We've done wheat then maize for as long as I can remember, same as everyone in the village.

For the wheat, I'll plant around October 10th like always, after we pull up the maize stubble. I buy the compound fertilizer from the village store — one bag of 复合肥 (compound, about 40 kg) before planting, that's about enough for my 1.8 mu. Then when the wheat greens up in spring around jointing time, I spread urea — maybe half a bag (25 kg) across the whole plot. My neighbor Wang dasao says she uses more but her land is better than mine.

I irrigate the wheat 3 times — once before winter so the roots don't freeze, once at green-up, and once at grain-filling if it doesn't rain. The well water costs money to pump, so I try not to do more than that. If the spring rain comes I skip one.

For maize, as soon as the wheat combine leaves — usually June 12-15, it's very tight — I spread some compound fertilizer and plant the same day with the neighbor's planter (I pay him 20 yuan/mu). I use a hybrid seed, Zhengdan or whatever the store has. Maize I don't irrigate unless it's really dry in July. One topdress of urea at the big trumpet stage.

I spray herbicide once on each crop because weeding by hand takes too long now that my back hurts. Pesticide only if I see bugs.

I expect maybe 400 jin of wheat per mu — that's 400 kg, about like last year — and similar from maize. Not as much as the big farmers but enough.
